## Today you will

- see an environment drift break a working command
- read a manifest and a lock file, and rebuild an environment from the lock file
- run the LTEE pipeline as Pixi tasks
- keep Linux-only tools away from Windows users without dropping them

## The same command, one year apart

```{.bash}
# 2025: FastQC 0.12.1
$ fastqc -o results/qc data/raw/fastq/*.fastq        # works

# 2026: FastQC 0.13.0
$ fastqc -o results/qc data/raw/fastq/*.fastq
fastqc: error: unrecognized arguments: -o
```

Your script did not change. **The environment did.**

> Full reproducibility requires the possibility to recreate the system that
> was originally used to generate the results. *(NBIS)*

## Package, dependency, environment

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- **package**: a program or library (`samtools`)
- **dependency**: what it needs to run, which needs more
- **environment**: one consistent set of packages, for one project

You ask for **17** packages. The lock file records **395** (pipeline
environment, Linux).
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
```{mermaid}
%%| eval: true
%%| echo: false
%%| fig-width: 7
flowchart LR
  subgraph env [pipeline environment]
    direction LR
    samtools --> htslib
    samtools --> ncurses
    htslib --> libcurl
    htslib --> libdeflate
    htslib --> bzip2
    htslib --> liblzma
    htslib --> libzlib
    samtools --> libzlib
    libcurl --> openssl
  end
```
:::
::::

## Where packages come from: channels

A **channel** is an online collection of packages.

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.key-box}
**bioconda**: bioinformatics software, built on top of conda-forge

`bwa` · `samtools` · `bcftools` · `fastqc` · `multiqc` · `snakemake` · `nextflow`
:::
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.key-box}
**conda-forge**: a community channel with tens of thousands of packages

`python` · `pandas` · `quarto` · `jupyterlab` · `graphviz`
:::
:::
::::

Pixi, Conda and Mamba all install from the same channels:
`channels = ["conda-forge", "bioconda"]` in `pixi.toml`.

## What you write vs what the machine records

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="45%"}
**`pixi.toml`** (you)

```{.toml}
[workspace]
channels = ["conda-forge", "bioconda"]
platforms = ["linux-64", "osx-arm64"]

[dependencies]
samtools = ">=1.24,<2"
```

intent: "any samtools 1.x from 1.24"
:::
::: {.column width="55%"}
**`pixi.lock`** (Pixi)

```{.yaml}
osx-arm64:
- conda: .../bioconda/osx-arm64/
    samtools-1.24-h36b3a25_2.conda
- conda: .../bioconda/osx-arm64/
    htslib-1.24-hd3c6ec9_0.conda
- ... every dependency
packages:
- conda: .../samtools-1.24-h36b3a25_2.conda
  sha256: f8ee1aea15b0b5...
```

fact: exact files and checksums, every platform
:::
::::

## Three commands

| Command | Does |
|---------|------|
| `pixi add samtools` | edits `pixi.toml`, updates `pixi.lock`, installs |
| `pixi run samtools ...` | runs one command in the project's environment |
| `pixi install --locked` | rebuilds exactly what `pixi.lock` says, or stops |

Delete `.pixi/` whenever you like: the lock file brings it back.

## Features: building blocks for environments

```{.toml}
[dependencies]                      # default feature: report tools, all platforms
quarto = ">=1.9"
pandas = ">=2"

[feature.pipeline]                  # bwa, samtools, bcftools: no Windows builds
platforms = ["linux-64", "osx-arm64", "osx-64"]

[feature.pipeline.dependencies]
bwa = ">=0.7.19,<0.8"
samtools = ">=1.24,<2"

[environments]
pipeline = ["pipeline"]             # = default + pipeline
```

## Tasks: the pipeline in one word

```{.bash}
$ pixi run reproduce
✨ Pixi task (download in default): python scripts/download_data.py
✨ Pixi task (qc in pipeline): fastqc ... && multiqc ...
✨ Pixi task (variant-calling in pipeline): bash scripts/run_variant_calling.sh
```

Each task runs in the environment that has its tools. The report joins
`reproduce` in lesson 07.

## GitHub reruns it on every push

```{.yaml}
- uses: actions/checkout@v7          # a clean clone
- uses: prefix-dev/setup-pixi@v0.11.2
  with: { locked: true }             # both environments, from pixi.lock
- run: pixi run reproduce            # download, QC, variant calling
```

The placeholder check from lesson 04 now does real work. Green check = your
project rebuilds **and reruns** on a computer that has never seen it.

## If you know Conda

| Conda | Pixi |
|-------|------|
| `environment.yml` (often written by hand) | `pixi.toml` (written by `pixi add`) |
| `conda env export > environment.yml` (if you remember) | `pixi.lock`, always up to date |
| `conda env create -f environment.yml` | `pixi install` (`--locked` for exactly the lock file) |
| `conda activate my-env` | `pixi shell`, or `pixi run COMMAND` |
| one environment per name, shared by projects | environments live in the project (`.pixi/`) |

Side by side, with commands: [tutorial 05b](../../pages/05b-conda-comparison.qmd).

## Conda, Anaconda, Miniconda, Miniforge...

| Name | What it is |
|------|------------|
| **conda** | the package and environment manager (open source) |
| **Anaconda** | the company; also a large installer and its `defaults` channel, which has commercial terms for bigger organizations |
| **Miniconda** | small conda installer, set to `defaults` |
| **Miniforge** | small conda installer, set to **conda-forge** (use this if you use conda) |
| **Mamba** | a faster reimplementation of conda |
| **Pixi** | project-based manager for the same packages, with lock files and tasks |

: {tbl-colwidths="[20,80]"}

## Think, pair, share {.prompt-slide}

::: {.prompt}
**3 minutes.** The lock file pins every package. List three things that can
still make your analysis give a different result on someone else's computer.
:::

::: {.notes}
Expected: hardware/OS and system libraries (glibc), the data, channels removing
packages, random seeds and thread counts, environment variables, time zones.
:::

## Quiz {.quiz-slide}

::: {.quiz}
1. Which file do you edit by hand? (a) `pixi.toml` (b) `pixi.lock` (c) both
2. `pixi install --locked` fails with "lock file not up-to-date". What changed? (a) the data (b) `pixi.toml` without a new `pixi.lock` (c) your internet
3. Why put bwa in a `pipeline` feature? (a) speed (b) it has no Windows build, and the report should still work on Windows (c) features are required
:::

::: {.notes}
Answers: 1 a; 2 b; 3 b.
:::

## Recap

- Manifest = intent; lock file = exact result, per platform. Commit both
- `pixi run` uses the project's environment; `--locked` rebuilds it exactly
- Features + environments handle tools that do not exist everywhere
- Tasks make the pipeline one command, locally and in CI
